items.why: Truist raised its price target to $1,000 on Tuesday and Pivotal raised its target to $930, both citing strong early adoption of Meta's Muse AI assistant ahead of Oct. 21 earnings.
Volatility is ticking up as chip stocks slide on AI spending fears and the broader market trades mixed at the start of earnings season.
Bitcoin bounced back above $83,000 after dipping under $81,000 overnight as a chip-led selloff in Korea rattled risk assets, then recovered as leveraged shorts were squeezed out.
Apple unveiled its HomeView smart home hub at a product launch event today, and JPMorgan raised its price target to $360 on Monday on a favorable holiday-quarter outlook.

market_note: CPI lands Wednesday morning, which could set the tone for the rest of the week.
summary: Stocks are trading mixed at midday as earnings season kicks off, with chip stocks sliding on AI spending fears while Meta and Apple rally on AI and product news.
